description: We want to know more about NASA's space exploration and we intend to present it in the best way possible. We are trying to uncover the hidden stories behind NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. We want to show you that these objects play a large role in NASA's journey.
summary:
What happens to spacecraft after their missions end? Although many NASA rovers, landers, and scientific instruments remain on the Moon and Mars, their remarkable stories and discoveries are often overlooked.

Lunar Legacy is an interactive educational website that brings these forgotten machines back to life through engaging digital storytelling. Designed for school-age space enthusiasts, our platform introduces historic NASA hardware, including the Apollo Lunar Modules, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, and Mars Pathfinder.

Through interactive mission timelines, Moon and Mars landing-site maps, spacecraft visualisations, and educational quizzes, users can explore how each machine functioned, what it discovered, and why its contributions remain important.

By combining scientific information with accessible storytelling and interactive learning, Lunar Legacy transforms retired space hardware into an engaging educational experience. Our project aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration, preserve awareness of NASA's scientific achievements, and encourage the next generation to become future scientists, engineers, and explorers.
details:
Lunar Legacy: Abandoned but Not Forgotten

1. Project Overview

Lunar Legacy is an interactive educational website developed to address the NASA Space Apps Challenge, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.”

Since the beginning of space exploration, NASA has sent numerous spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments to explore other worlds. Although many of these machines have completed their missions and remain on the Moon or Mars, their extraordinary achievements continue to contribute to our understanding of space.

Our project aims to bring these machines' stories to life, making space exploration more engaging, accessible and meaningful for school-age students.

Rather than simply presenting historical facts, Lunar Legacy transforms scientific information into interactive storytelling experiences that allow users to discover each spacecraft's mission, understand how its equipment functioned and appreciate the legacy it left behind.

2. How Our Project Works

The website follows three main learning stages:

MEET — Discover the Hardware

Users are introduced to NASA's historic spacecraft through engaging storytelling hooks, mission descriptions and visual representations. Featured missions include Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Mars Pathfinder, Phoenix and the Apollo lunar missions.

EXPLORE — Follow the Mission

Users explore the spacecraft's journey, operational purpose and scientific discoveries through interactive features, including:

  • Mission Explorer: Browse spacecraft and learn about their roles, destinations and achievements.
  • Moon and Mars Maps: Select landing sites to discover where specific missions operated and what equipment remains there.
  • 3D Spacecraft Visualisations: Rotate and zoom into interactive spacecraft representations, with explanations of their components and functions.
  • Interactive Storytelling: Follow missions through their launch, exploration, scientific discoveries and lasting legacy.
  • Mission Timeline: Explore important milestones in the history of lunar and Martian exploration.

REMEMBER — Understand the Legacy

Users discover why each mission remains scientifically significant, even after its operations have ended. An educational quiz reinforces what they have learned and encourages active participation.

3. Tools and Technologies Used

Lunar Legacy was developed as a web-based educational platform using:

  • GitHub: To organise the website's source code and support online publishing.
  • Canva: To design visual storytelling materials and presentation content.
  • Netlify: To publish.

The project also draws upon NASA's publicly available mission information and educational resources to support its scientific storytelling.

4. Creativity and Innovation

Lunar Legacy combines science, history, technology and storytelling into a unified educational experience.

Its key creative concept is to treat spacecraft as the central characters of their own stories. Each machine is introduced through an engaging question or narrative hook, followed by explanations of its mission, scientific purpose and discoveries.

By integrating interactive 3D visualisations, landing-site maps, mission timelines and educational quizzes, the website encourages users to become active explorers rather than passive readers.

The project also highlights an important perspective: a spacecraft's scientific legacy does not end when its mission ends.

5. Intended Benefits and Impact

Lunar Legacy is designed primarily for school-age students, educators and young space enthusiasts.

The project aims to:

  • Make NASA's historical missions easier for students to understand.
  • Encourage curiosity about astronomy, planetary science, robotics and engineering.
  • Help learners understand the relationship between scientific instruments and important discoveries.
  • Promote interactive, self-directed learning.
  • Inspire young people to pursue future opportunities in STEM education and space exploration.

By presenting complex scientific concepts through accessible stories and interactive experiences, Lunar Legacy aims to make space science engaging for learners with different backgrounds and levels of knowledge.

6. Design Considerations

During development, our team considered the importance of scientific accuracy, age-appropriate language, ease of navigation, visual engagement and accessibility.

We organised the website around the simple learning journey of Meet, Explore and Remember, helping students progress from discovering a spacecraft to understanding its scientific contributions.

We also considered compatibility with commonly used web browsers and the importance of making educational content accessible without requiring specialised equipment.

7. Conclusion

Lunar Legacy demonstrates how digital storytelling can preserve and communicate the achievements of historic NASA missions.

By bringing together scientific information, interactive technology and creative storytelling, our project transforms retired space hardware into an educational experience for the next generation.

Our message is simple:

“Abandoned does not mean forgotten. The mission may end, but the discovery continues.”
